 The autonomous vehicle appears to slow down on the turn as the girl steps onto the road towards it.

 Set as preferred source Listen Summarise 中文 Grab is reviewing a near-accident in Punggol, where a girl almost was hit by an autonomous vehicle making a left turn at a green light.
 A video on Facebook showed the AV not stopping before the crossing; a woman pulled the girl away. The clip has more than 260,000 views.
 Grab said, “Safety is our top priority,” and it is working with the Land Transport Authority and WeRide. The case comes after an earlier AV crash nearby in January.
 AI generated
 SINGAPORE – Grab has been directed to stop testing its autonomous vehicles (AVs) in certain scenarios in Punggol, as the Land Transport Authority (LTA) investigates a near-accident there between one such vehicle and a girl.
 A video of a Grab AV almost hitting a girl crossing the road while it was making a left turn was posted on Facebook on the night of Nov 5, and has since attracted much attention. A woman can be seen accompanying the girl in the video.
 In response to media queries, LTA said it was informed of the incident on Nov 5 and is investigating the case.
 The authority said the vehicle was testing a new route in preparation for enhanced on-demand travel within Punggol, a service that is expected to be expanded to the wider public in the fourth quarter of 2026 .
 “Preliminary data indicates that the vehicle had detected the two pedestrians, and was continuously tracking the pedestrians’ movements,” LTA said.
 It pointed out that the vehicle turned left after the traffic light turned green, and that the pedestrians were stationary for some time at first.
 According to LTA, the vehicle started braking and steered away to the right when the child began crossing the road. The safety operator on board then took over control of the vehicle, continued to brake and steered the vehicle away from the pedestrian.
 “LTA has directed Grab to pause testing at such junctions until investigations are completed, and we will review whether the response to such scenarios should be adjusted,” the authority said.
 It thanked the public for sharing the video and reminded pedestrians to watch for oncoming traffic to completely stop before crossing roads.
 In the uploaded video, as the vehicle approaches the pedestrian crossing, a girl on the pedestrian walkway to the vehicle’s left steps off the kerb to cross the road.
 The traffic lights are green for both the pedestrian and the AV at this point.
 The AV appears to slow down on the turn as the girl steps onto the road towards it, and the girl halts as the vehicle drives past in front of her.
 A woman can be seen approaching the girl and pulling her away from the vehicle.
 The vehicle then appears to slow down before moving off.
 The video has since garnered over 260,000 views and 1,000 reactions.
 A comparison between the video and Google Maps shows that the incident occurred in Punggol Field Walk.
 The location is near the site of another accident involving an AV in January, in which the AV collided with a road divider .
 In response to media queries, a Grab spokesperson said the company is aware of the latest incident.
 “Safety is our top priority. We are aware of this incident and are closely reviewing it together with the Land Transport Authority (LTA) and our partner WeRide,” the spokesperson said.
 Grab’s AV shuttle services have been available to the public since April 1.
 It operates two shuttle routes in Punggol, with one connecting Punggol Matilda Court and Oasis Terraces, and the other connecting Punggol Matilda Court and Punggol Coast Mall.
 In an announcement in July, Grab said it would trial letting people book AV rides between specific pickup and drop-off points along its existing routes in the following months.
